result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B says not now to all three ideas more consistently and sticks to fewer levers. Its claim that $8–10 a board in costs would pull the rate toward $15/hr is wrong: it would be about $20–21/hr. A has the stronger pricing analysis and the concrete 30-hour subscription example, but it adds more levers, gives tier advice and ends with a step-by-step plan, which makes it less conversational. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A gives a firm 'not yet' on all three ideas and grounds it in the roughly 67 hours a month. It also reads the per-hour figures correctly: they are nearly the same across sizes, and it ties any price change to the cost of materials. B's arithmetic is right too, but it says the pricing 'has a problem' when the hourly rates differ only slightly, and it is less firm on tiers. B is also longer and more structured, with a step-by-step plan, though its suggestion of a modest price rise plus paid upgrades fits the levers item well.
